newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus leader confirms defence minister in office.
newsitem.headline: Belarus leader confirms defence minister in office.

text.p: Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko confirmed the permanent appointment on Saturday of his previously acting defence minister, General Alexander Chumakov, a presidential spokesman told Reuters.
"The president today signed a decree and appointed Chumakov defence minister," a spokesman said by telephone.
Chumakov, former chief of the general staff of Belarus's 100,000-strong armed forces, had been acting defence minister since last November.
He took over from General Leonid Maltsev, who was sacked by Lukashenko for turning up drunk at a public function.

Chumakov has sharply criticised NATO's plans to admit former communist countries in eastern Europe, including Belarus's western neighbour Poland. He also favours closer military ties between Belarus and Russia.

Belarus allows Moscow to keep several military bases on its territory in return for cheaper oil and gas from Russia. Last November, Russia removed the last Soviet-era strategic nuclear missile from Belarussian territory.
Lukashenko, commenting on his plans for new government appointments, said on Friday that many ministers would go.
